newsitem.title: USA: Molecular, Lockheed in fiber optic pact.
newsitem.headline: Molecular, Lockheed in fiber optic pact.

text.p: Molecular OptoElectronics Corp said it and Lockheed Martin's Communications and Power Center agreed to collaborate on developing fiber optic technology to transmit high-speed microwave signals.

Lockheed Martin would use the technology for commercial satellite and defense-related applications, while Molecular would engage in commercial markets for terrestrial communications, the company said.
Molecular, which is privately-held, also said it would supply components to Lockheed Martin for their systems.

"We are pleased to join forces with a company of the caliber of Lockheed Martin to develop the kinds of solutions that their defense and aerospace customers are seeking," Molecular President Kevin Stewart said.
"We are well aware that commercial carriers also have their own pressing needs, and we look forward to meeting their demands for greater bandwidth," he said.

The development pact related to a new class of fiber optic modulators, devices which encode data onto the laser beam in an optical fiber. These modulators would be able to impart high-frequency microwave signals onto a fiber link, it said.
Molecular said the high-frequency capability would open large market for both it and Lockheed Martin.
Lockheed said the pact was a key step in developing next-generation satellites to meet demand for space-based telecommunications.
